steps.name: prompt
steps.text: Write the introduction for our paper on ModeT, a motion decomposition Transformer for deformable medical image registration. It should set up the registration problem, review how Transformers have been used for registration and where they fall short, and list our contributions.

steps.name: skeleton_outline
steps.text:
- Deformable image registration: importance and problem formulation
- Registration as voxel correspondence, similar to Transformer computation
- Transformers in medical image registration and their limitations
- The few works linking attention and deformation estimation
- Our method: ModeT and experiments
- Contributions

steps.name: detailed_outline
steps.text:
- Deformable registration
  - important focus in medical imaging; preoperative planning, intraoperative information fusion, disease diagnosis, follow-ups (cite)
  - goal: solve non-rigid deformation field to warp moving image -> warped image anatomically similar to fixed image
  - notation: I_{f},I_{m}\in\mathbb{R}^{H\times W\times L} fixed/moving images (H,W,L image size)
  - deep-learning paradigm: spatial transformer network (STN) (cite) applies sampling grid G\in\mathbb{R}^{H\times W\times L\times 3} to moving image
  - G = regular grid + deformation field
- Registration = correspondence
  - for p\in\mathbb{R}^{3}, G(p): voxel at p in fixed corresponds to voxel at G(p) in moving
  - so registration = finding corresponding voxels -> relative positional relationship between voxels
  - very similar to calculation method of Transformer (cite)
- Transformers in registration
  - successful in computer vision, recent impact in medical image computing (cite)
  - registration nets using Transformers to enhance structure: Transmorph, Swin-VoxelMorph, Vit-V-Net (cite each)
  - problem: only self-attention to boost feature learning (as in segmentation), not designed for registration
  - cross-attention for moving/fixed correspondence: Attention-Reg, Xmorpher (cite each)
  - cross-attention Transformer (CAT) module: bottom layer of Attention-Reg, each layer of Xmorpher
  - still limited to feature learning; no consideration of attention vs deformation estimation
  - Xmorpher: large network -> only small windows for similarity calculation -> possible performance degradation
- Attention + deformation estimation (few works)
  - Coordinate Translator, Deformer (cite)
  - Deformer: attention map x Value matrix used to weight predicted basis -> deformation field; but attention map only concatenation + projection of moving/fixed features, no similarity calculation
  - Coordinate Translator: matching score of fixed and moving feature maps, scores re-weight deformation field
  - but at coarse-level resolution a voxel often has multiple possible motion modes (cite) -> not considered by Coordinate Translator
- ModeT
  - novel motion decomposition transformer; explicitly models multiple motion modalities; exploits Transformer's intrinsic capability for deformation estimation
  - experiments: two public brain MRI datasets; beats several cutting-edge registration networks and Transformers
- Contributions
  - Transformer structure models correspondence -> deformation field; separates feature extraction and deformation estimation; more sensible procedure
  - multi-head neighborhood attention for multiple motion modalities; competitive weighting module (CWM) fuses deformation sub-fields competitively; interpretability, consistency
  - pyramid structure for feature extraction + deformation propagation; reduces attention scope per level

steps.name: partial_draft
steps.text:
Deformable image registration is an important focus in medical imaging, and it is essential for preoperative planning, intraoperative information fusion, disease diagnosis and follow-ups. The goal of deformable registration is to solve the non-rigid deformation field that warps the moving image, so that the warped image becomes anatomically similar to the fixed image. Let I_{f},I_{m}\in\mathbb{R}^{H\times W\times L} be the fixed and moving images (H,W,L denote image size). In deep-learning-based registration, a spatial transformer network (STN) is usually needed to apply the estimated sampling grid G\in\mathbb{R}^{H\times W\times L\times 3} to the moving image. G is obtained by adding the regular grid and the deformation field. For any position p\in\mathbb{R}^{3} in the sampling grid, G(p) gives the corresponding relation, which means the voxel at position p in the fixed image corresponds to the voxel at position G(p) in the moving image. So image registration can be seen as finding the corresponding voxels between the moving and fixed images and turning this into the relative positional relationship between voxels, and this is very similar to the way a Transformer calculates things.

Transformers have been used successfully in computer vision and recently they also had an impact in medical image computing. In medical image registration there are also several studies that use Transformers to enhance the network structure and get better registration performance, for example Transmorph, Swin-VoxelMorph and Vit-V-Net. But these networks mostly just use the self-attention mechanism of Transformers to boost feature learning, the same as segmentation tasks do, and they are not really designed for registration. Some other methods use cross-attention to model the correspondence between the moving and fixed images, such as Attention-Reg and Xmorpher. Attention-Reg uses the cross-attention Transformer (CAT) module in its bottom layer and Xmorpher uses it in each layer, to build the relationship between the moving and fixed image features. But these two methods still only use the Transformer to improve feature learning, and they do not consider the relationship between the attention mechanism and deformation estimation. Also, because the network structure of Xmorpher is large, only small windows can be made for the similarity calculation, and this may make the performance worse.

- Attention + deformation estimation (few works): Coordinate Translator, Deformer
  - Deformer: attention map x Value matrix weights predicted basis -> deformation field; attention map only concat + projection, no similarity calculation
  - Coordinate Translator: matching score of fixed/moving feature maps re-weights deformation field
  - coarse resolution: voxel has multiple motion modes, not considered by Coordinate Translator
- ModeT: motion decomposition transformer, explicit multiple motion modalities; two public brain MRI datasets, beats cutting-edge networks and Transformers
- Contributions
  - Transformer models correspondence -> deformation field; separates feature extraction / deformation estimation
  - multi-head neighborhood attention; competitive weighting module (CWM) fuses sub-fields; interpretability, consistency
  - pyramid structure; smaller attention scope per level

steps.name: rough_draft
steps.text:
Deformable image registration is an important focus in medical imaging, and it is essential for preoperative planning, intraoperative information fusion, disease diagnosis and follow-ups. The goal of deformable registration is to solve the non-rigid deformation field that warps the moving image, so that the warped image becomes anatomically similar to the fixed image. Let I_{f},I_{m}\in\mathbb{R}^{H\times W\times L} be the fixed and moving images (H,W,L denote image size). In deep-learning-based registration, a spatial transformer network (STN) is usually needed to apply the estimated sampling grid G\in\mathbb{R}^{H\times W\times L\times 3} to the moving image. G is obtained by adding the regular grid and the deformation field. For any position p\in\mathbb{R}^{3} in the sampling grid, G(p) gives the corresponding relation, which means the voxel at position p in the fixed image corresponds to the voxel at position G(p) in the moving image. So image registration can be seen as finding the corresponding voxels between the moving and fixed images and turning this into the relative positional relationship between voxels, and this is very similar to the way a Transformer calculates things.

Transformers have been used successfully in computer vision and recently they also had an impact in medical image computing. In medical image registration there are also several studies that use Transformers to enhance the network structure and get better registration performance, for example Transmorph, Swin-VoxelMorph and Vit-V-Net. But these networks mostly just use the self-attention mechanism of Transformers to boost feature learning, the same as segmentation tasks do, and they are not really designed for registration. Some other methods use cross-attention to model the correspondence between the moving and fixed images, such as Attention-Reg and Xmorpher. Attention-Reg uses the cross-attention Transformer (CAT) module in its bottom layer and Xmorpher uses it in each layer, to build the relationship between the moving and fixed image features. But these two methods still only use the Transformer to improve feature learning, and they do not consider the relationship between the attention mechanism and deformation estimation. Also, because the network structure of Xmorpher is large, only small windows can be made for the similarity calculation, and this may make the performance worse.

Only a few studies consider the relationship between attention and deformation estimation, such as Coordinate Translator and Deformer. Deformer uses the transformer's way of multiplying the attention map with the Value matrix, and uses it to weight the predicted basis and generate the deformation field. But its attention map is only computed by concatenating and projecting the moving and fixed feature maps, and there is no similarity calculation part. Coordinate Translator calculates the matching score between the fixed feature map and the moving feature map, and then the scores are used to re-weight the deformation field. However, for feature maps at coarse-level resolution a voxel often has several possible motion modes, and this is not considered in Coordinate Translator.

In this study we propose a new motion decomposition transformer (ModeT) that explicitly models multiple motion modalities by fully using the intrinsic ability of the Transformer structure for deformation estimation. We did experiments on two public brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) datasets, and they show that our method does better than several cutting-edge registration networks and Transformers. Our main contributions are:

- We use the Transformer structure to naturally model the correspondence between images and convert it into the deformation field. This explicitly separates the two tasks of feature extraction and deformation estimation in deep-learning-based registration networks, which makes the registration procedure more sensible.

- ModeT uses the multi-head neighborhood attention mechanism to model multiple motion modalities efficiently, and then the competitive weighting module (CWM) fuses the multiple deformation sub-fields in a competitive way. This can improve the interpretability and consistency of the deformation field we get.

- We use a pyramid structure for feature extraction and deformation propagation, which helps to reduce the scope of attention calculation needed at each level.

steps.name: revised_draft
steps.text:
Deformable image registration has always been an important focus in the medical imaging community, and is essential for preoperative planning, intraoperative information fusion, disease diagnosis and follow-ups [1,2]. Deformable registration solves the non-rigid deformation field used to warp the moving image, so that the warped image becomes anatomically similar to the fixed image. Let I_{f},I_{m}\in\mathbb{R}^{H\times W\times L} be the fixed and moving images (H,W,L denote image size). In the deep-learning-based registration paradigm, a spatial transformer network (STN) [3] is often employed to apply the estimated sampling grid G\in\mathbb{R}^{H\times W\times L\times 3} to the moving image, where G is obtained by adding the regular grid and the deformation field. For any position p\in\mathbb{R}^{3} in the sampling grid, G(p) represents the corresponding relation, i.e., the voxel at position p in the fixed image corresponds to the voxel at position G(p) in the moving image. In other words, image registration can be understood as finding the corresponding voxels between the moving and fixed images and converting this into the relative positional relationship between voxels, which is very similar to the calculation method of Transformer [4].

Transformers have been successfully used in computer vision and have recently made an impact in medical image computing [5,6]. In medical image registration, several studies also employ Transformers to enhance network structures for better registration performance, such as Transmorph [7], Swin-VoxelMorph [8] and Vit-V-Net [9]. However, these networks often merely leverage the self-attention mechanism in Transformers to boost feature learning (as segmentation tasks do), without sufficient design for the registration task. Other methods use cross-attention to model the corresponding relationship between moving and fixed images, such as Attention-Reg [10] and Xmorpher [11]. The cross-attention Transformer (CAT) module is used in the bottom layer of Attention-Reg [10] and in each layer of Xmorpher [11] to establish the relationship between the features of moving and fixed images. However, the usage of Transformer in [11,10] is still limited to improving feature learning, with no additional consideration of the relationship between the attention mechanism and the deformation estimation. Moreover, due to the large network structure of [11], only small windows can be created for similarity calculation, which may lead to performance degradation. Few studies consider the relationship between attention and deformation estimation, such as Coordinate Translator [12] and Deformer [13]. Deformer [13] uses the Transformer's multiplication of the attention map and Value matrix to weight the predicted basis and generate the deformation field, but its attention map is only computed by concatenating and projecting the moving and fixed feature maps, without a similarity calculation. Coordinate Translator [12] calculates the matching score of the fixed and moving feature maps, and the computed scores are then employed to re-weight the deformation field. However, for feature maps with coarse-level resolution, a voxel often has multiple possible motion modes [14], which is not considered in [12].

In this study, we propose a novel motion decomposition transformer (ModeT) to explicitly model multiple motion modalities by fully exploiting the intrinsic capability of the Transformer structure for deformation estimation. Experiments on two public brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) datasets show that our method outperforms several cutting-edge registration networks and Transformers. The main contributions of our work are summarized as follows:

- We propose to leverage the Transformer structure to naturally model the correspondence between images and convert it into the deformation field, thus explicitly separating the two tasks of feature extraction and deformation estimation in deep-learning-based registration networks and making the registration procedure more sensible.

- The proposed ModeT makes full use of the multi-head neighborhood attention mechanism to efficiently model multiple motion modalities, and the competitive weighting module (CWM) then fuses multiple deformation sub-fields in a competitive way, improving the interpretability and consistency of the resulting deformation field.

- A pyramid structure is employed for feature extraction and deformation propagation, which helps reduce the scope of attention calculation required at each level.
